{{Short description|German plant physiologist}}

'''Eberhard Schäfer''' (born 23 June 1945) is a German [[plant biologist]] and professor emeritus at the [[University of Freiburg]]. He is recognized for his contributions to the study of phytochromes, light perception in plants, and photomorphogenesis.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1369526603000827 | doi=10.1016/S1369-5266(03)00082-7 | title=Light perception and signalling in higher plants | date=2003 | last1=Gyula | first1=Péter | last2=Schäfer | first2=Eberhard | last3=Nagy | first3=Ferenc | journal=Current Opinion in Plant Biology | volume=6 | issue=5 | pages=446–452 | pmid=12972045 | bibcode=2003COPB....6..446G | url-access=subscription }}</ref> His work has combined experimental biology with mathematical modeling and has contributed to the understanding of plant light signaling pathways, including photoreceptor-mediated nuclear import and thermal sensing in plants.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=EZhch-MAAAAJ&hl=de | title=Google Scholar }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Eberhard Schäfer was born in [[Thuringia]], [[East Germany]], and grew up in [[Lower Saxony]] and later in [[Duisburg]], where his father worked in the oil trade.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web| title=ASPB Pioneer Member - Eberhard Schäfer | url=https://aspb.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/ASPBPioneerMember_EberhardSchafer.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705150145/https://aspb.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/ASPBPioneerMember_EberhardSchafer.pdf | archive-date=2022-07-05}}</ref> Initially interested in medicine and the physical sciences, Schäfer studied [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] at the University of Freiburg.<ref name="Mitglieder">{{Cite web | title=Mitglieder | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/eberhard-schaefer/ | access-date=2025-08-21 | website=www.leopoldina.org}}</ref> After completing his Diplom (equivalent to a master’s degree) in physics in 1969<ref>{{Cite web| title=Curriculum Vitae Professor Dr. Eberhard Schäfer | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Schaefer_Eberhard_D.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201025050358/https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Schaefer_Eberhard_D.pdf | archive-date=2020-10-25}}</ref> he transitioned into [[biology]], with an interest in [[photobiology]].
He began his doctoral research in the laboratory of [https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Mohr Hans Mohr] at the University of Freiburg. Schäfer’s PhD work focused on in vivo [[spectroscopy]] of [[phytochrome]] using the [[Ratiospect]] device, a semi-automated photometric system. He completed his doctorate in 1971 and was offered a permanent research position shortly thereafter.<ref>{{Cite web| title=ASPB Pioneer Member - Eberhard Schäfer | url=https://aspb.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/ASPBPioneerMember_EberhardSchafer.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705150145/https://aspb.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/ASPBPioneerMember_EberhardSchafer.pdf | archive-date=2022-07-05}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Schäfer established an independent research group at Freiburg and received his [[habilitation]] in 1975.<ref name="Mitglieder"/> In 1995 he was  appointed as a full professor,<ref name="Mitglieder"/> succeeding Hans Mohr. 
He has held sabbatical appointments at institutions including with [[Winslow Briggs]] in the [[Carnegie Institute of Science|Carnegie Institute]] at [[Stanford]]<ref>{{Cite web | title=Remembering Winslow Briggs {{!}} Carnegie Science | url=https://carnegiescience.edu/NASBriggs | access-date=2025-08-21 | website=carnegiescience.edu}}</ref> and with Masaki Furuya at the [[RIKEN]] Institute<ref>{{Cite web| title=Masaki Furuya - ASPB Corresponding Member, University of Tokyo | page=16 | url=https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2014/septoct14.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018141510/http://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2014/septoct14.pdf | archive-date=2017-10-18}}</ref> in Japan.

== Research contributions ==
Schäfer’s research spans multiple domains of plant photobiology:

=== Phytochrome kinetics and mathematical modeling ===
* Developed mathematical models describing the kinetics of phytochrome action, including continuous light responses (High Irradiance Response, HIR).<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00276015 | doi=10.1007/BF00276015 | title=A new approach to explain the ?high irradiance responses? Of photomorphogenesis on the basis of phytochrome | date=1975 | last1=Schäfer | first1=E. | journal=Journal of Mathematical Biology | volume=2 | pages=41–56 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Demonstrated the temperature dependence of phytochrome dark reversion, contributing to later research showing that phytochrome B (phyB) functions as a thermosensor.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.aaf6005 | doi=10.1126/science.aaf6005 | title=Phytochromes function as thermosensors in ''Arabidopsis'' | date=2016 | last1=Jung | first1=Jae-Hoon | last2=Domijan | first2=Mirela | last3=Klose | first3=Cornelia | last4=Biswas | first4=Surojit | last5=Ezer | first5=Daphne | last6=Gao | first6=Mingjun | last7=Khattak | first7=Asif Khan | last8=Box | first8=Mathew S. | last9=Charoensawan | first9=Varodom | last10=Cortijo | first10=Sandra | last11=Kumar | first11=Manoj | last12=Grant | first12=Alastair | last13=Locke | first13=James C. W. | last14=Schäfer | first14=Eberhard | last15=Jaeger | first15=Katja E. | last16=Wigge | first16=Philip A. | journal=Science | volume=354 | issue=6314 | pages=886–889 | pmid=27789797 | bibcode=2016Sci...354..886J | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.aaf5656 | doi=10.1126/science.aaf5656 | title=Phytochrome B integrates light and temperature signals in ''Arabidopsis'' | date=2016 | last1=Legris | first1=Martina | last2=Klose | first2=Cornelia | last3=Burgie | first3=E. Sethe | last4=Rojas | first4=Cecilia Costigliolo Rojas | last5=Neme | first5=Maximiliano | last6=Hiltbrunner | first6=Andreas | last7=Wigge | first7=Philip A. | last8=Schäfer | first8=Eberhard | last9=Vierstra | first9=Richard D. | last10=Casal | first10=Jorge J. | journal=Science | volume=354 | issue=6314 | pages=897–900 | pmid=27789798 | bibcode=2016Sci...354..897L | hdl=11336/25099 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

=== Nuclear import of phytochromes ===
* In collaboration with Ferenc Nagy identified and characterized the light-dependent nuclear import of phytochromes (types A–E), which helped link photoreception at the plasma membrane or cytosol to nuclear gene expression.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1105/tpc.11.8.1445 | title=Light Quality–Dependent Nuclear Import of the Plant Photoreceptors Phytochrome a and B | date=1999 | last1=Kircher | first1=Stefan | last2=Kozma-Bognar | first2=Laszlo | last3=Kim | first3=Lana | last4=Adam | first4=Eva | last5=Harter | first5=Klaus | last6=Schäfer | first6=Eberhard | last7=Nagy | first7=Ferenc | journal=The Plant Cell | volume=11 | issue=8 | pages=1445–1456 | pmid=10449579 | pmc=144301 | bibcode=1999PlanC..11.1445K }}</ref>
* Collaborated with Ferenc Nagy and others to demonstrate how post-translational modification of phytochromes modifies  intracellular localization dynamics and signaling.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Medzihradszky |first1=Mátyás |last2=Bindics |first2=János |last3=Ádám |first3=éva |last4=Viczián |first4=András |last5=Klement |first5=éva |last6=Lorrain |first6=Séverine |last7=Gyula |first7=Péter |last8=Mérai |first8=Zsuzsanna |last9=Fankhauser |first9=Christian |last10=Medzihradszky |first10=Katalin F. |last11=Kunkel |first11=Tim |last12=SchÄfer |first12=Eberhard |last13=Nagy |first13=Ferenc |date=2013-03-26 |title=Phosphorylation of Phytochrome B Inhibits Light-Induced Signaling via Accelerated Dark Reversion in Arabidopsis |journal=The Plant Cell |language=en |volume=25 |issue=2 |pages=535–544 |doi=10.1105/tpc.112.106898 |issn=1532-298X |pmc=3608776 |pmid=23378619|bibcode=2013PlanC..25..535M }}</ref>

=== UV-B photoreception ===
* Collaborated with Klaus Hahlbrock and later with Roman Ulm and Ferenc Nagy among others on the mechanisms of UV-B perception.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid=24212345 | date=1989 | last1=Ohl | first1=S. | last2=Hahlbrock | first2=K. | last3=Schäfer | first3=E. | title=A stable blue-light-derived signal modulates ultraviolet-light-induced activation of the chalcone-synthase gene in cultured parsley cells | journal=Planta | volume=177 | issue=2 | pages=228–236 | doi=10.1007/BF00392811 | bibcode=1989Plant.177..228O }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1200660 | doi=10.1126/science.1200660 | title=Perception of UV-B by the ''Arabidopsis'' UVR8 Protein | date=2011 | last1=Rizzini | first1=Luca | last2=Favory | first2=Jean-Jacques | last3=Cloix | first3=Catherine | last4=Faggionato | first4=Davide | last5=o'Hara | first5=Andrew | last6=Kaiserli | first6=Eirini | last7=Baumeister | first7=Ralf | last8=Schäfer | first8=Eberhard | last9=Nagy | first9=Ferenc | last10=Jenkins | first10=Gareth I. | last11=Ulm | first11=Roman | journal=Science | volume=332 | issue=6025 | pages=103–106 | pmid=21454788 | bibcode=2011Sci...332..103R | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* Contributed to the identification and characterization of [[UVR8]] as a specific UV-B photoreceptor.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.1200660 | doi=10.1126/science.1200660 | title=Perception of UV-B by the ''Arabidopsis'' UVR8 Protein | date=2011 | last1=Rizzini | first1=Luca | last2=Favory | first2=Jean-Jacques | last3=Cloix | first3=Catherine | last4=Faggionato | first4=Davide | last5=o'Hara | first5=Andrew | last6=Kaiserli | first6=Eirini | last7=Baumeister | first7=Ralf | last8=Schäfer | first8=Eberhard | last9=Nagy | first9=Ferenc | last10=Jenkins | first10=Gareth I. | last11=Ulm | first11=Roman | journal=Science | volume=332 | issue=6025 | pages=103–106 | pmid=21454788 | bibcode=2011Sci...332..103R | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Honors and memberships ==
* Member of the German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina (since 2001).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/eberhard-schaefer/ | title=Mitglieder }}</ref>
* Recognized as an ASPB Pioneer Member by the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]]<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://aspb.org/membership/aspb-pioneer-members/pioneer-testimonials/eberhard-schafer-testimonials/ | title=Eberhard Schäfer Testimonials }}</ref>
